title: MZ Chains of Destiny: Captive in Another World - Dark Fantasy RPG

posts.author: World_Creator
posts.body:
Chains of Destiny: Captive in Another World​
Engine: RPG Maker MZ  |  Status: Playable Demo (First 5 Minutes)
Spoiler:
SYNOPSIS
"The story is of a person who is like you and me, spending his life peacefully with his mother. But he is unknown of what is coming at him, and what he will become in the future... ...and where will his destiny take him?"
Chains of Destiny follows an ordinary young man named Mark — not a hero, not a chosen one. Just a normal person living a quiet life with his mother, carrying the quiet grief of a father who vanished without explanation years ago.
But the world around them is changing. Strange news reports warn of people disappearing across the region. When his mother's medicine runs out, Mark makes the difficult choice to step outside despite the danger — a small errand that will change everything.
The ground shakes. A nearby building collapses. A glowing blue portal tears open from within the rubble, and soldiers from another world pour through — clad in strange armor, speaking a language Mark cannot understand. He tries to run. He tries to fight. He fails. Beaten and unable to breathe, he loses consciousness.
He wakes up in a cold, dark prison cell. In another world. Alone.
The villain & the reason​
In this other world, a powerful and ruthless figure is building something — a creation so dangerous that it would make him completely unstoppable. But to finish it, he needs two things: slaves to do the work, and a massive power source to fuel it.
He turned to the nations of his own world first. Some refused. Those who agreed eventually ran out of people to send. With no more slaves available in his own world, he found another solution — he built a device capable of tearing open portals to other worlds and dragging their people through by force.
People from our world — people like Mark — were chosen deliberately. Not just as workers, but because humans from our world carry a natural strength and energy that the villain needs to power his creation. Mark is not special. He is not a chosen hero. He was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. And now he is a prisoner in a world he never knew existed, trying to do one thing: survive and find a way home.
The world​
The game is set in a dark fantasy world — but with a strange and unsettling twist. Because the two worlds are now colliding due to the portal device, pieces of Mark's world have begun appearing in this strange land. Familiar things like a "Modern City Inn" or an "Urban Mart" stand oddly in the middle of this dark and dangerous place. These are not just decoration — they are clues to a deeper mystery about what is happening to both worlds, and perhaps, a key to finding Mark's way home.
About Mark​
Mark is not your typical RPG hero. He does not want to save the world. He is afraid, he is overwhelmed, and more than anything — he just wants to go home to his mother. His journey is not about becoming a warrior or a saviour. It is about a frightened, ordinary person trying to survive in an impossible situation, and maybe, if he is lucky, finding answers along the way.
Gameplay features​
World exploration — Walk through different maps, find items, and uncover clues about the two colliding worlds.
Turn-based battles — Fight dangerous enemies using the classic RPG battle style.
Story-driven mystery — Uncover why the worlds are colliding, who the villain is, and how Mark might escape.
Meaningful choices — Small decisions during the story that reflect Mark's personality as a normal, fearful person.
Playable demo — A 5-minute gameplay slice showing the very beginning of Mark's journey.
Credits & tools used​
Engine: RPG Maker MZ
Assets: Default RPG Maker MZ Graphics and Music
Cover art: Hand-made original art by the developer
Other tools: YouTube (for devlogs) and Aseprite (for future art)

Does the story opening feel interesting and emotional to you?
Is the dialogue easy to understand and follow?
Does the idea of a villain with a real, selfish reason make the story feel more believable?
Does Mark feeling like a normal, scared person rather than a hero feel fresh or different to you?
